newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Ample supplies drag down prices.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Ample supplies drag down prices.

text.p: Singapore gas oil resisted crude's rise, weakening on ample supplies and limited buying interest, traders said on Thursday.
No trades were done on Thursday, but sellers lowered their offers down to between $22.60-$22.85 per barrel, compared to offers at above $23.00 on Wednesday.
Traders said that the shutdown of Indonesia's Cilacap refinery for maintenance is expected to have a limited impact on the market, as Indonesia had already covered the bulk of its requirements.
The refinery started a 35-day maintenance shutdown of its 100,000 barrels-per-day crude distillation unit from Wednesday.
A September buy tender by Nepal Oil Corp (NOC) will be awarded by late Thursday, traders said.
They said that the best offer was submitted by German trader Mabanaft, at around $176.99 per tonne, with the next best offer coming from Japanese trader Tomen, at $177.15 per tonne.
This is higher than the award made in Nepal's last tender, where it bought two August cargoes, from Shell at $162.69 per tonne, and from BB Energy at $163.44.
But traders said that the August tender had been awarded at a time when the overall gas oil prices were at historical lows, explaining the aggressive offers.
Activity on the jet market was thin, without any buying inteest sighted.
Traders said that it was getting difficult to play the physical/paper price differential since there was already a large volume of jet in storage.

"There's two million barrels of jet in storage in Singapore, and probably another one and a half million in Guam, and more in Jebel Ali. There's a lot of jet around," said a trader with a major oil company.
Some traders had earlier bought jet cargoes at low levels to be stored, making a profit by selling paper at higher prices.
Jet was offered at a wide range of $22.90 to $24.10 for end August/early September.
But no bids emerged.
